rule: Call through a parameter, local variable or stored property holding a function (callback, closure, fn pointer, delegate) → callee is the variable's name, `call_type` callback, confidence unknown. | `this.x` assigned a value is a callback. | **unknown**: a dynamic call (function value, callback, closure, function pointer). | Not calls: passing a method reference (`x::m`, `self.m` without call), enum-variant/data construction (Rust `Some(x)`, `E::V(..)`, Haskell `Con {..}`), casts, language constructs (`isset`, `empty`, `sizeof`), declarations/function heads, module attributes, typespecs, field access without a call. | Anonymous functions, lambdas, object-literal methods and anonymous-class members fold into the nearest enclosing named function (or the module/type at top level). A caller is never empty.
notes: `fn(x)` calls a parameter; `this.onClick()` calls a stored property assigned a value in the constructor ('`this.x` assigned a value is a callback'), callee is the property name `onClick`; `chosen(...)` calls a local bound to a call result. All callback/unknown with the variable's name. `b` is bound by `= new Button(...)` so `b.click()` is `cb.Button#click` (decision A, high because defined in scan). `each` on line 17 and `handler` passed as an argument on lines 22-23 are references, not calls. `handler(v)` inside the anonymous arrow folds into `cb.run`.
